content_html:
When time is short, a home looks and feels cleaner if you prioritize what guests see, touch, and use: the entry, bathroom, clear surfaces, sink, and main traffic floors. Do not attempt a whole-house deep clean. Work in sequence, carry a basket for misplaced items, and leave hazardous or long-drying tasks for another time.

Start by decluttering rather than scrubbing

Walk through common areas with a basket and collect clothing, mail, toys, and items that do not belong there. Put the basket away to sort later; clear surfaces make the actual cleaning much faster.

Do the guest bathroom and kitchen sink

Clean the sink, toilet, mirror, and touch points; restock paper and provide a clean hand towel. In the kitchen, empty or organize the sink and wipe visible counters. Do not mix cleaners when moving between rooms.

Dust only the visible surfaces

Tables, living-room furniture, and eye-level shelves have more impact than the top of a cabinet. Use a microfiber cloth and work from higher to lower surfaces so loose dust reaches the floor before vacuuming.

Finish with traffic paths and a brief airing-out

Vacuum or sweep the entry, living area, and path to the bathroom; mop only if needed and if the floor can dry before people arrive. Air the space safely for a few minutes when outdoor conditions allow rather than masking odors with heavy fragrance.
